documents.title: A randomized control trial evaluating the effects of police body-worn cameras
documents.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
documents.quote: we show that BWCs have very small and statistically insignificant effects on police use of force
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Finds no reduction in use of force, opposing claim.

documents.title: Community Perceptions of Police Body-Worn Cameras
documents.quote: recent research suggests positive impacts of BWCs on reducing police use-of-force and citizen complaints
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Abstract only reports perceptions, not empirical effect on force.

documents.title: Police Body-Worn Cameras: Perceptions of Law Enforcement Leadership
documents.quote: command staff believe BWCs will impact police officers’ decisions to use force in encounters with citizens and police will be more reluctant to use necessary force
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Reports beliefs, not measured reduction in force.

documents.title: Police Body-Worn Cameras: Effects on Officers’ Burnout and Perceived Organizational Support
documents.quote: We find BWCs increase police officer burnout, and this effect is statistically different from zero.
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Focuses on officer burnout, not on use of force.

documents.title: The Achilles Heel of Police Body-Worn Cameras: Understanding the Factors That Influence Variation in Body-Worn Camera Activation
documents.quote: Our analysis suggests that a wide variety of individual, situational, organizational, and neighborhood factors are related to an officer’s decision to activate their camera
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Focuses on camera activation, not force outcomes.

documents.title: The Influence of Defendant Race/Ethnicity and Police Body-Worn Cameras on Traffic Case Processing
documents.quote: BWCs did significantly reduce the likelihood of a guilty plea for Black and White defendants
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Addresses traffic case outcomes, not use of force.

documents.title: Testing the Evidentiary Value of Police Body-Worn Cameras in Misdemeanor Court
institutions: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
documents.quote: BWCs did not affect case flow but did affect processing and outcomes for most cases.
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Discusses case processing, not use of force.

documents.title: Automation and artificial intelligence in police body-worn cameras: Experimental evidence of impact on perceptions of fairness among officers
documents.quote: Automatic BWC activation and artificial intelligence auditing of footage cause declines in perceived fairness of monitoring.
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Examines perceived fairness, not use of force.

documents.title: Police Body-Worn Cameras
documents.quote: Although research testing the efficacy of body cameras is inconsistent
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Discusses discourse, no empirical force data.

documents.title: THE COMPARISON OF POLISH AND GERMAN MODELS FOR THE UTILISATION OF POLICE BODY-WORN CAMERAS
documents.quote: In Poland, the public discourse focused on the use of this technology to reduce the (ab)use of coercive measures by police officers.
documents.verification_scope: Quotation verified, not independent validation of the interpretation.
documents.why: Describes policy discourse, no empirical findings on force reduction.

stats.sentence: At the same time, before–after analyses show that assaults were overall reduced by 61% in the participating police departments, thus suggesting paradoxical effects.

source.title: Paradoxical effects of self-awareness of being observed: testing the effect of police body-worn cameras on assaults and aggression against officers

stats.sentence: A total of 394 assaults per 1000 arrests occurred during 3637 treatment shifts (M = 39.35, SD = 17.89) compared with 284 assaults per 1000 arrests during 3697 control shifts (M = 28.38; SD = 15.99), which translate into 37% higher odds of assault in treatment shifts than in control conditions.

stats.caveat: substantially more pronounced in low discretion sites
stats.sentence: The backfiring treatment effect was substantially more pronounced in low discretion sites, i.e., where officers strongly followed the experimental protocol (OR = 2.565; 95% CI 1.792, 3.672).
